context: Since revealed vertices need not all be requested, we distinguish between ∆G , the maximum degree of the full revealed graph, and ∆, the maximum degree of G[Vn ], the subgraph induced by requested vertices. In Section 4.1, we present an O(log2 ∆G )-competitive deterministic algorithm for the unweighted case, for both incremental DS and incremental CDS. Then, in Section 4.2, we show that in the weighted case there exists an O(log n log ∆)-competitive deterministic algorithm for incremental DS. We leave improving the upper bound for weighted incremental CDS as an open problem. This model differs from that of [14], where a vertex must be covered only when its last neighbor is revealed, and late acceptance is disallowed. 4.1 Unweighted Case We first present a deterministic algorithm for incremental DS. Our approach is based on maintaining both a fractional solution and an integral dominating set D, coupled through a potential function. The potential function penalizes vertices that are covered fractionally but not integrally, ensuring that vertices with high fractional coverage are added to the integral solution.
